notes: Temple Run is the named reference and forward motion is automatic, so Infinite Runner and its genre-wide P6; the skyscrapers are the setting, not a second genre. The answer settles the genre's real fork on three fixed lanes, which is lane-snap and therefore Lane Runner's own shape with no substitution needed — I rejected traversal-city, which is the catalogue's rooftop shape, because it assumes a freely crossed city with the streets below as a fallback route and costs P2, whereas here the rooftops are a single scrolling play surface and a fall ends the run. Kept chunk-modular and collectible-nodes as the Temple Run coin-trail read, dropped obstacle-moving since the answer rules out a chaser and nothing else moves, and added obstacle-jump for the gaps between buildings and hazard-kill for the drop that ends a run. Without a user I decided the streets far below are backdrop rather than a second walkable layer, so no P2, took the stylized cartoon New York look from the answer, and used settlement-density for the dense skyscraper block grid the rooftop course runs across.
